recommendations.task: Fast whole-body and implement-adjacent shop motion with an eventual six-to-eight-camera volume.
qualification_gates: Obtain complete comparable quotes and exact SDK EULAs.
Measure two-camera exposure skew, drops, jitter, and sustained full-rate payload.
Measure pose and triangulation error throughout the intended volume under shop lighting and occlusion.
Verify lens field of view, working distance, focus lock, exposure, blur, and lighting safety.
Scale the proven topology to six and eight cameras without sharing an unqualified USB bottleneck.
recommendations.decision: Buy two cameras for the pilot, not the full rig. Start with the FLIR candidate when temporal sampling is the priority; select the Basler alternate when the pilot proves its extra pixels materially improve keypoint localization at 160 fps.
recommendations.limitations: This is an engineering-screen recommendation, not procurement approval or a claim of biomechanical accuracy.

recommendations.task: Larger or cable-constrained capture volume where rugged synchronized GMSL2 links are more important than full-resolution sampling above 60 fps.
qualification_gates: Confirm the exact full-resolution frame rate required by every intended task.
Benchmark the complete capture-card and NVIDIA compute topology with the intended camera count.
Review proprietary SDK, driver, model, redistribution, and hardware lock-in terms.
Measure pose accuracy against the fast-motion pilot rather than assuming depth or vendor synchronization improves it.
recommendations.decision: Keep the ZED X One GS as a topology evaluation, not the default fast-motion purchase. Its synchronized GMSL2 architecture is attractive for long cable runs, but full-resolution video is limited to 60 fps and the stack adds capture-card, NVIDIA, fixed-lens, and proprietary-SDK constraints.
recommendations.limitations: No physical comparison, price-normalized quote, or open-core adapter has been completed.
